questions.prompt: A client casually says “all these poverty mindset” about society, not about you. You freeze and try to prove you are not poor. What did you do?
options: Personalize a statement that was not directed at you. Listen to context; contribute briefly if appropriate; do not turn the massage into a debate about your finances.
Ask the client how much they earn.

questions.prompt: The client uses “poverty mindset” because you actually cut a corner in the service. What is the well-resolved path?
options: Argue that the label is always abusive.
Identify the reason, fix the issue, apologize, and make clear it was an error, not your identity.
Ignore the service error and only refuse the words.
Offer an unauthorized discount from fear.

questions.prompt: The client harshly concludes you are poor as a personal judgment. What does the article require?
options: Accept the label to keep the peace.
Vehemently refuse the label. Make it clear you are not poor, not part of poverty territory, and do not operate under that mindset. Stay professional. Escalate if disrespect continues.
Badmouth the client after the session.

questions.prompt: You ration oil below the standard because you fear lack of supplies. What is forming?
options: Scarcity producing fear of using resources even when they are legitimately required, and cutting corners because of fear of lack.

questions.prompt: A wealthy client books Combo. You feel smaller and become stiff. What is the right mindset line?
options: “I can serve wealthy people without feeling inferior.” Someone else's wealth is not evidence of your inferiority.
“I should ask for extra money privately.”
“I should reduce my pressure to match my income.”

questions.prompt: A colleague succeeds and you look for faults so you feel better. What question should you ask?
options: “Can I acknowledge another person's success without needing to explain it away?”

questions.prompt: Need tempts you to weaken a boundary with a client who tips well. What must you refuse?
options: Allowing financial need to weaken professional boundaries. Do not allow personal need to reduce professional standards.

questions.prompt: You serve a client who appears to have less money with less care. What did you violate?
options: Nothing if they booked a shorter service.
“I can serve people with less without treating them as less important.”

questions.prompt: You badmouth a client in the staff area because of what they own. How does the article name this?
options: Badmouthing clients because of what they own, spend or request — a scarcity-produced behaviour.

questions.prompt: You notice jealousy rising after a colleague's compliment. What is the closing cycle?
options: Notice → Question → Correct → Learn → Improve → Serve professionally.

title: SECTION B — FILL IN THE GAP

required to hide from wealthy clients.

questions.prompt: The Goal list includes which instruction?
options: Identify with poverty so you stay humble.
Do not identify with poverty. Do not reflect scarcity in service. Drop associated midsts as soon as you notice them.
Treat poorer-looking clients as less important.
Use need to justify extra-boundary service.

questions.prompt: Seeing clients as “people who have money” rather than people you are professionally serving is listed as…
options: a behaviour scarcity can start producing.

questions.prompt: The right mindset includes: “When I notice jealousy, envy, inferiority or scarcity thinking, I…”
options: identify it quickly and correct it.

questions.prompt: The remember line says you should refuse harsh personal judgment…
options: by leaving the spa without reporting.
by agreeing so the client calms down.
